Every Bell Agrees

Speech Functions · Ask four people · Record what you would say

THE DIRECTIONS

You will talk to four people. Record what you would say to each one. You can record again as many times as you want. When all four are recorded, click Submit.

The first time you press record, your computer will ask to use your microphone. Click Allow.

The sign

As you record, the four numbers fill in. Multiply the waves each second by the length of one wave.

THE SCENE

Your class put two old bells in a glass box in the school hall. You are making the sign that tells people about them. You are alone in the workroom, and the sign is empty. You need four numbers, and four people each have one.

THE HISTORY

This bell came from a carillon, a tower with many bells. The Hemony brothers made carillons in the Netherlands in the 1600s. They were the first to make bells with the exact sound every time. Their bells are still in towers today.
